support-agent-ella: Escalation from ACME. Their rerank requests sometimes return 502 or nonsensical score distributions when payloads include emoji clusters + some control characters. Repro case attached from their staging traffic (sensitive redacted).

customer-acme-tester: Repro steps (from our side):
```
# node test script that streams chunks
const http = require('http');
const req = http.request({ method: 'POST', path: '/v1/rerank', headers: { 'Transfer-Encoding': 'chunked', 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Authorization': 'Bearer REDACTED' } });
req.write('{"query":"Which astronaut is", "docs":["I saw the star 👩‍🚀','\u0000']');
// intentionally split multi-codepoint emoji across writes
req.write('\uD83D');
setTimeout(() => { req.write('\uDC69\u200D\uD83D\uDE80"}] }'); req.end();
```
We see two behaviours: 1) 502 from the rerank service; 2) when it returns 200, the scores are inconsistent (the doc with the emoji gets very low score compared to identical doc without it).

ingrid-eng-ml: I reproduced locally. When the UTF-8 for the sequence crosses a chunk boundary we end up with a partial byte sequence hitting the tokenizer/byte-level hash -> different tokenization -> different scores. On top of that, our pipeline currently rejects some partial sequences and bubbles up a 502 from the decoder.

jack-eng-runtime: Logs from the serving side (trimmed):
```
E decoder: invalid utf-8 sequence at offset 768
E rerank: handler error: upstream decode error -> 502
```
Looks like our ingress layer leaves chunked bodies to be reassembled by the app. In our test, the proxy is forwarding chunk boundaries without ensuring proper reassembly into a single UTF-8 buffer before tokenization.

maria-devex: Customer noted this only happens when they stream via an old corporate proxy. Non-streaming (Content-Length) requests are fine. They can't easily change the proxy.

ingrid-eng-ml: Two issues to fix: 1) Do not allow tokenization on partial byte sequences. Reassemble and validate UTF-8 before any tokenization/hash. 2) Normalize/sanitize invalid sequences to U+FFFD for best-effort scoring rather than failing outright, with a metric so we can detect noisy inputs.

jack-eng-runtime: Proposed quick mitigation (patch):
- At ingress: accumulate chunked body into buffer up to X MB (streamed limiter), run a single UTF-8 validation pass. If invalid sequences found: either return 400 with code `invalid_encoding` OR replace invalid runs with U+FFFD if customer opts into best-effort via header `X-Redwood-encoding: best-effort`.
- At router/proxy: ensure it doesn't hand off partial buffers to the model worker.

support-agent-ella: Customer wants a hotfix because it impacts production batches. Can we triage to P1?

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026, assigned to eng-runtime. Pager duty notified.

jack-eng-runtime: I'll push a small hotfix to the ingress validation. Plan: add a UTF-8 reassembly + validation middleware in front of the rerank handler, defaulting to returning 400 for malformed UTF-8. If ACME needs tolerant mode, we'll add header. I can have a canary patch on staging in ~2 hours.

ingrid-eng-ml: Also adding regression test to the rerank eval suite: stream-splitting tests with multi-codepoint emoji, ZWJ sequences, and embedded control chars + NUL. We should assert deterministic tokenization vs non-chunked path.

maria-devex: I'll draft an email for ACME explaining the cause (chunk boundaries splitting UTF-8) and the short-term workaround (use Content-Length or set header to request tolerant mode once live).

support-agent-ella: Thanks. Action items: (1) jack -> ingress hotfix P1 (2) ingrid -> add regression tests (3) maria -> customer comms. I'll follow up in INC-2026. :thumbsup:
